definition: A hedge is equal in size and risk to the investment it offsets, but in practice it often receives far less organizational review and oversight than the original investment decision.
core_idea: A major capital investment might get extensive committee-level review, while the equally large, directionally-opposite hedge position offsetting it may be designed by a single junior employee with only cursory senior-management review.
key_points: A hedge carries the same magnitude of risk as the position it offsets
Investment decisions are typically reviewed by many stakeholders
Hedge design/execution can be delegated with much lighter review, creating an oversight gap
This asymmetry in scrutiny is itself identified as a risk management issue
trading_implications: Firms should apply governance/review rigor to hedge construction proportional to its size, not just to the original investment
